title: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds

result.label: Erdős reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial density bounds
result.statement: Every set A of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for every fixed k≥3 there are constants C_k, c_k, ε_k > 0 such that r_k(N) ≤ C_k N exp(−c_k(log N)^(ε_k)), where r_k(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,…,N} with no nonconstant k-term progression.
result.detail: Corollary 1.2 is the reciprocal-sum consequence of Theorem 1.1. The Lean comparator is named for the reciprocal-sum theorem; the quantitative density bound has no alignment recorded here.
result.roleNote: The density bound is the main theorem. The reciprocal-sum statement is its corollary, obtained by summing the bound over dyadic intervals.

strategies.label: Main paper · 198 pp

nodes.label: Interval inverse theorem
nodes.fullLabel: External input · Leng–Sah–Sawhney interval inverse theorem
nodes.detail: A quantitative interval inverse theorem for the uniformity norm, used in the comparison and return estimates of §7. It is an external analytic input, not proved in this paper.

nodes.label: Radius-sensitive almost periodicity
nodes.detail: The radius-sensitive almost-periodicity theorem supplies the shift comparison used in §7. It is an external analytic input, not proved in this paper.

nodes.label: Pathwise detection
nodes.detail: Prescribes finitely many testing degrees for a constrained path law and detects a positive density increment along active paths, with approximation in the mixed ambient cube norm.

nodes.label: Prepared system by rank cuts
nodes.fullLabel: Proposition 4.1 · Prepared system with triangular costs
nodes.detail: Rank cuts prepare a triangular two-box certificate while preserving the box certificate and controlling the relative loss of each width. Backward rank transfer and relative rank-cut transactions are the main inputs.

nodes.label: Detection independent of width
nodes.fullLabel: §5 · Detection independent of the current width
nodes.detail: Bounded-grid moments and relative cube detection densify without paying the chart mass, so the detection estimate does not depend on the current width.

nodes.label: Forward mass
nodes.detail: Forward sampling of a prepared cell transfers the density certificate to terminal boxes and yields an absolute increment, with the selected planes and flags kept under control.

nodes.label: Scalar comparison and return
nodes.detail: Comparison measure, forecasts, and passive-layer returns quantify the relative width loss while preserving old equations. The interval inverse theorem and radius-sensitive almost periodicity enter the comparison machinery here.

nodes.label: Active replacement
nodes.detail: Active globalization replaces the active modulus and produces an exact marked projection, preserving the structural data needed for the next round.

nodes.label: One-layer extraction
nodes.detail: Extracts the next cell, preserves old equations, and controls the new width budgets. Flags and inactive equations are removed, with real pivots and boundary losses localized.

nodes.label: Triangular increment
nodes.detail: A density certificate on a triangular cell yields a new cell with fresh absolute slots and controlled precision and width loss. The absolute starting rule adds only polynomially many determining coordinates, so the fresh rank is dimension-independent.

nodes.label: Triangular iteration
nodes.detail: Iterates the increment, closes the triangular dimension, width, and finite-horizon recurrences, and derives the density contradiction at the endpoint.

nodes.label: Quasipolynomial density bound
nodes.detail: For each fixed k≥3 there are constants C_k, c_k, ε_k > 0 such that r_k(N) ≤ C_k N exp(−c_k(log N)^(ε_k)) for every N≥2.

nodes.label: Divergent reciprocal sums
nodes.detail: Every set A of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length. The proof sums the density bound over dyadic intervals [2^m,2^(m+1)).

sharedInputs: Triangular polynomial cells and density certificates
Precision and width budgets indexed by weight
The constrained path law and its detection estimates
The interval inverse theorem and radius-sensitive almost periodicity
summaryNote: A section-level spine of a 198-page proof. The density bound is the main theorem; the reciprocal-sum corollary is the consequence formalized upstream. Many internal lemmas and appendices are intentionally grouped.

leanAlignments.note: The comparator theorem name matches the paper's reciprocal-sum corollary. The Lean statement and proof were not kernel-checked or independently reviewed here; the quantitative density bound is outside this alignment.

caveats: Section-level map of a 198-page proof. Nodes group many lemmas and appendices; the paper remains authoritative.
The interval inverse theorem and radius-sensitive almost periodicity are external analytic inputs. Their cited statements and hypotheses are not re-proved or independently reviewed here.
The Lean comparator is aligned to the reciprocal-sum corollary, not to the quantitative density bound. Fetching the module is not a kernel build or a Proofweave replay.
Unreviewed: no statement review, independent review, or contribution receipt.
